characters.description: The titular protagonist who aspires to become a true hero. The Ace: Once he completes his training under Phil and starts picking up wins over monsters, Hercules quickly develops this status and reputation among the people of Thebes. The "Zero to Hero" musical number is all about his rise to fame and throughout the song, the Muses talk him up as aShowy Invincible Hero, aNice Guy, aChick Magnet, and aHumble Herowith much public love. Adaptational Dumbass: In the myths, Herakles is well educated, a successful military commander by his late teens, an occasional trickster, and a master ofIndy Ploys. The Disney Hercules, while by no means stupid and showing occasional moments of guile, comes off as rather airheaded, naive, klutzy and uncultured in comparison. Adaptational Nice Guy: By modern standards, the Hercules of Greek mythisn't exactly a paragon of heroic virtue. He kills more than one innocent person simply for being too close when his temper gets the better of him (although he's alwaysremorsefulwhen this happens), andhe stages a HUGE war for a mere verbal insult at one point, although he does go to great lengths to help his friends and his deeds do the world a lot of good. This Hercules is a friendly, wide-eyed boy scout who doesn't have many, if any, vices. The worst thing he does is lash out at Phil and slap him for trying to warn him about Meg being in league with Hades, but he immediately comes to regret that. Adaptation Name Change: In the Greek myth, his name is written as "Herakles". "Hercules" is theLatin pronunciation, which is more widely recognizable to modern viewers.

characters.name: Hercules
characters.description: The titular protagonist who aspires to become a true hero. The Ace: Once he completes his training under Phil and starts picking up wins over monsters, Hercules quickly develops this status and reputation among the people of Thebes. The "Zero to Hero" musical number is all about his rise to fame and throughout the song, the Muses talk him up as aShowy Invincible Hero, aNice Guy, aChick Magnet, and aHumble Herowith much public love. Adaptational Angst Downgrade:Zig-Zagged. Compared to his mythological counterpart, who had Hera attempting to kill him his entire life for being the product of one of Zeus' (many) affairs and slew his own children after being driven mad by said stepmother, his life was downright peaceful. However, his struggles with controlling hisSuper-Strengthare given a much greater focus in his backstory here, where he was shunned in his youth for accidentally causing destruction with his clumsiness, while Hercules in the myth in his youth managed to find a place where his strength could be put to use without being a danger to anyone else and earned acceptance there. On the other hand, Hercules in the myth also accidentally killed his music teacher after striking him too hard in response to a scolding, while this Hercules' bouts of accidental destruction never killed anyone. characters.name: Megara
characters.description: The female lead of the movie. A jaded, sarcastic woman who works under Hades and falls in love with Hercules. Adaptational Backstory Change: In Greek mythology, Megara is the daughter of King Creon of Thebes, making her a princess. There's no mention of Meg being descended from royalty in the film. Adaptational Villainy: Downplayed. The original Megara in Greek myth never worked for Hades, or was associated with any villainous figures in general (though the mythological Hades wasn't evil to start with). Here, she's initially introduced as Hades' disgruntled henchwoman. Age-Gap Romance: Her age isn't specified (unlike Hercules, whose being eighteen is a plot point), but it's implied that she's a fair bit older than him. She refers to him as "junior" when they first meet. The midquel animated series reveals that she's close to his age (she went on a blind date with his classmate, Adonis, and she and Hercules lost their memory of their first meeting when they got accidentally drenched in the Lethe water she enlisted his help in retrieving), but its canonicity is debatable. And in the stage musical, she's already an adult working for Hades when Hercules is just a baby, with it also being stated that she's completely immortal as long as Hades has her soul. Annoying Laugh: On seeing Hercules's high school photo, she lets out a cacophonous cackle that Phil calls her out on.

characters.name: Philoctetes
characters.description: A satyr and Hercules' trainer. Adaptation Species Change: He was human in the original myth. Here, he's a satyr. The stage musical reverses this however, and reimagines him as a human gyro seller (or pub employee in later productions). Age Lift: In the original myth, he was a child when Hercules died. Disney's portrayal of him makes him significantly older, enough to have trained many figures of Greek Mythology. Ascended Extra: Philoctetes was barely involved in the original Heracles myth, only playing a part in it after Hercules had died. The Disney movie bumps him up to a major role as Hercules' trainer. Badass Teacher:Downplayed; he teaches Hercules to fight monsters but runs away when monsters actually show up. He's no coward, though — he frequently stays nearby and goads Hercules to keep on fighting like a coach. Phil is smart enough to know that, being the stubby satyr he is, he's completely outmatched by the monsters Herc fights and would be immediately in over his head if he actually tried to fight alongside him. Although even if he can't fight monsters, he's still strong enough to easily beat the crap out ofhumanmen several times his size.

characters.name: Pegasus
characters.description: The flying horse companion of Hercules. Adaptational Backstory Change: The mythological Pegasus was born from the blood of Medusa's decapitated head, and served as the mount for the hero Bellerophon. In this movie, he's created from clouds by Zeus to be a present for the baby Hercules. Animals Lack Attributes: He's meant to be a stallion, as shown by his falling for theHoney Trapmade by Pain and Panic shapeshifting as a mare, but he lacks a sheath or testicles. Also, despite having a prominent butt crack, he lacks an anus, which would have been seen clearly when he was trying to force his butt through Phil's door. Ass Kicks You: He performs mild examples of this a couple of times, which arePlayed for Laughs:After flying Hercules and Meg to the canyon to save the two trapped boys, he hears Meg ask for help getting off lest she “ruin the upholstery” by vomiting, so he bucks his rear end up to force her off into Hercules’ arms.When he and Phil retrieve Hercules from his date with Meg, Hercules is too lovestruck to pay attention and walks backwards while waving bye to her, so Pegasus aims with his hind leg and uses his butt to bounce Hercules onto his back. After flying Hercules and Meg to the canyon to save the two trapped boys, he hears Meg ask for help getting off lest she “ruin the upholstery” by vomiting, so he bucks his rear end up to force her off into Hercules’ arms.

characters.name: Amphitryon and Alcmene
characters.description: Hercules' adoptive parents who raised him after he was taken from his home on Mount Olympus. Adaptational Wimp: The Amphitryon of myth was a famed soldier and a hero in his own right. Here, he's just an elderly farmer, mainly to be an analogue toJonathan Kent. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: At least how Hercules saw them in his teens because they would talk frankly to others of life on the farm instead of tales of adventure or excitement. Cassandra reminds him that every teenager would rather kiss a Gorgon than be seen in public with their parents, but Hercules insists that this is somehow different. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Amphitryon has these and due to age they are also white. Chubby Mama, Skinny Papa: Overweight Alcmene and her skinny husband Amphitryon, respectively.

characters.name: Icarus
characters.description: Hercules' best friend during their time in Prometheus Academy. He also has a romantic obsession with their friend Cassandra. Abhorrent Admirer: To Cassandra. She regards him as a nuisance. Granted, heisbrain damaged, so it's difficult for him to take a hint.Circe took a liking to him, only to lose interest the moment they reached her home. Circe took a liking to him, only to lose interest the moment they reached her home. All Men Are Perverts: His interaction with Cassandra borders on harassment. Attention Deficit... Ooh, Shiny!: His attention can swap from the topic at hand to the ridiculously mundane at the drop of a hat.

characters.name: Cassandra
characters.description: She is a close friend of Hercules and to a lesser extent Icarus, who is hopelessly in love with her, during their time in Prometheus Academy. Keep in mind,try not to confuse her withtheotherCassandraofanother Disney animated seriesnor thatother onefromanother unrelated fighting game series. Adaptational Nationality: The mythical Cassandra was Trojan (specifically, she was Hector and Paris's sister), not Athenian. Canon Foreigner: Like Icarus up there, she's TV series only. Can't Live with Them, Can't Live Without Them: Icarus may be anAbhorrent Admirer, but Cassandra feels a void when Icarus is gone for alongtime.

characters.name: Adonis
characters.description: A snobbish prince of Thrace and recurring bully for Hercules. Animal Stereotypes: Unsurprisingly, he's turned into a peacock in "Song of Circe". Big Jerk on Campus: A handsome and popularRoyal Bratwho enjoys making fun of Hercules and anyone else he deems below him.Even Herc has a hard time standing him. The Bully: He enjoyed humiliating Hercules and his friends during their time at Prometheus Academy. Bullying a Dragon: In the series, it's common knowledge that Herc's the son of Zeus, and that he has super strength. Why he still bullies Herc is anyone's guess.

characters.name: Helen of Troy
characters.description: The most popular girl at Prometheus Academy. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She has a notable attraction to powerful or unpleasant men, as seen with her constant relationship with Adonis despite being a jerkass snob and a later stated attraction to Orion the Hunter for his macho and hairy persona. She does provide affection to Hercules though not enough to formally be with him in a relationship. Brainless Beauty: Helen of Troy. Her face launched a thousand ships, not her head. Class Princess: A nice and friendly cheerleader. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Helen has blonde hair and is an absolute sweetheart.

characters.name: Daedalus
characters.description: The shop class teacher at Prometheus Academy, famed inventor, and Icarus' father. He is far wiser than his son, though about as eccentric. Absent-Minded Professor: Daedalus is incredibly intelligent and sharp, but when he gets to inventing everything else around him tends to vanish. This allows villains like Minos to get him to make them something dangerous without Daedalus questioning them until its too late. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Aloof and often impatient, he still wants his students to succeed. In particular he will get fed up and impatient with Hercules, but refuses to give up on him and wants to help him learn. Papa Wolf: He is incredibly protective of Icarus, as well as Hercules. Minos finds this out the hard way.

characters.name: Orpheus
characters.description: The hottest singer in Greece, Orpheus is aTeen Idolof considerable renown who frequently plays sold-out concerts. He was mentioned offhand in the movie before appearing in person in the animated series. Adapted Out: There's no mention of the other famous half of his myth: his lover Eurydice. British Rockstar: Orpheus speaks with an English accent and is the most popular singer in Greece. Hidden Depths: According to Hermes in the movie, he's also good at flower arrangements. Rescued from the Underworld: In a twist on the trope maker, Orpheus himself has to be rescued when Hades kidnaps him for a concert.

characters.name: Tempest
characters.description: A warrior and princess of the Amazons. The Ace: A very skilled Amazonian warrior, who is able to throw a spear. Action Girl: It's not uncommon to see her accompanying Hercules (or Hercules being in her way) and doing a better job in tasks. All Amazons Want Hercules: Averted, as she's never shown romantic feelings towards Hercules. In fact, when she first meets him in "Hercules and the Assassin", she's unimpressed and doesn't open up to him (though this is mostly due to her strict upbringing). By the end of the episode, she shows respects towards him. Anime Hair: Her ponytail is shaped like the horsehair crest on top of a helmet, which showcases her war-like personality.

characters.name: Chipacles
characters.description: Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He is a blunt and stern cop who is still a sincerely good guy. He is just as likely to help Herc as get in his way. Pet the Dog: Chipalces may get on Herc's case a lot, but he shows frequently he can lighten up and be aReasonable Authority Figure.InHercules and the Driving Test, Hercules basically stops the sun to give himself more time to complete his driving test. Chipacles is perfectly okay with this unusual loophole and is willing to let Hercules finish the test.Chiplaces is ready to punish Hercules for sneaking into a tavern despite being underaged for most ofHercules and the Epic Adventure, but after Hercules saves the city from Orthos he is willing to look the other way.He is quick to team up with both Herc and Phil inHercules and Disappearing Heroes, even letting Hercules take the lead when he gets a good plan. At the end of the episode he is seen bowling with them now, admitting he thinks they are okay in his book now. InHercules and the Driving Test, Hercules basically stops the sun to give himself more time to complete his driving test. Chipacles is perfectly okay with this unusual loophole and is willing to let Hercules finish the test. Chiplaces is ready to punish Hercules for sneaking into a tavern despite being underaged for most ofHercules and the Epic Adventure, but after Hercules saves the city from Orthos he is willing to look the other way. He is quick to team up with both Herc and Phil inHercules and Disappearing Heroes, even letting Hercules take the lead when he gets a good plan. At the end of the episode he is seen bowling with them now, admitting he thinks they are okay in his book now.

characters.name: Chiron
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: Chiron in the original Greek myth was famous for being the only gentle centaur. Here, Chiron acts just as aggressively and arrogantly as all the other centaurs we see. Always Someone Better: It is initially believed he is the better hero trainer than Phil is. This is ultimately subverted though; Phil's star student ultimately proves he is far better than evenChiron himself. Decomposite Character: In Greek mythology, Chiron was the trainer who taught most of the greatest heroes, including Heracles, Jason, and Achilles. In the movie's continuity, all three were taught by Philoctetes, so the spinoff show portrays Chiron as Phil's obnoxious rival who trained someReal Lifefigures from ancient history, as well asthe Biblical Samson.

characters.name: Bob the Narrator
characters.description: A mysterious, presumably mortal voice that narrates the adventures of Hercules and friends. Bob is on good terms with the Muses despite their frequent narrative takeovers, and has a wife named Mrs. Bob, a daughter named Tiffany and a son named Chad. Adam Westing: His name Bob is a shortened nickname for Robert, implying that the show's narrator really is Robert Stack interacting with the Greek world. How this connects to the Charlton Heston narrator from the movie, if it does at all, is unknown. Ascended Extra: The Narrator in the movie serves as more of a gag to introduce the muses. He only has a few lines before they take over and isn't heard from after he hands the story off to them. In the series, he has much more extended interactions with the muses and frequently covers smaller bits of exposition. Bob usually has more lines in an episode than he did in the entire movie. The Fourth Wall Will Not Protect You:Played for Laughswhen Circe hypnotizes Bob to stop him from pointing out how evil and manipulative she is and switch it so that he's complimenting her. Lemony Narrator: Bob often interacts with the Muses in the episode openings.

characters.name: Odysseus
characters.description: King of Ithaca and Hercules’ most favorite hero that he looks up to and aspires to be. He was a former student of Phil. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: Telemachus isn’t mentioned in the opening narration and Odysseus himself admits to Hercules that his son is around the latter’s age, i.e early teens. This means he became a parentafterreturning home and got to be a part of his son's life from the get-go. There’s also no mention of him ever gettingimprisoned by Circe and/or Calypso. Babies Ever After: After reuniting with Penelope, they went on to have Telemachus. Badass in Distress: Hercules accidentally trapping him into Hecate’s clutches leads to him getting imprisoned and his cunning stolen away. Crazy Jealous Guy: Odysseus isnotpleased when Penelope admits that she had a lot of suitors pursuing her while he was away from home. When he angrily questions why he’s only finding out about it now, Penelope reveals that he already killed them, to which Odysseus admits he thought they were salesmen.

characters.name: Cerberus
characters.description: Hades' giant three-headed dog, who guards the entrance to the Underworld. Adaptation Expansion: Not an enormous one, but he gets more screentime in the animated series as a puppy. He also appears as a reoccuring boss in theKingdom Heartsseries. Angry Guard Dog: He's anenormous dogwho guards the entrance to the Underworld. Beware of Vicious Dog: He actually snarled at Hades as he entered, though he is later pacified when being given a large piece of steak (that’s tiny from their perspective) by Hades. Canis Major:Oh boy is he!He's even larger thanClifford!

characters.name: Nessus
characters.description: A centaur whom Hades sent Megara to recruit. Abhorrent Admirer: He has hots for Megara, who obviously doesn't reciprocate. Adaptational Wimp: Downplayed. The mythological Nessus was the one responsible for Heracles' death thanks to the centaur's poisonous blood, but it was aMutual Kill, and Heracles only died shortly after killing Nessus. In the film proper, he gets only one good hit in before Herculescurb-stomps him. Amazing Technicolor Population: Nessus has blue skin a few shades lighter than the fur covering his lower body. Cranial Eruption: He's left with a massive welt on his head, which his horseshoes land on.

characters.name: Hydra
characters.description: A two-legged serpentine dragon with the ability to grow back multiple heads for every one that's cut off. 2D Visuals, 3D Effects: It's animated with CG instead of traditional 2D animation. Alien Blood: Hercules decapitates the Hydra dozens of times during their battle, which is shown in full, unusually gory detail for a Disney movie. But since the Hydra happens to have green blood, the scene is still family-friendly despite the violence depicted. Ambiguous Gender: Most sources refer to the Hydra as "it". Phil's dialogue in the film and read-along storybook refers to the Hydra with masculine pronouns ("Dance around him!"), and he suggests calling it "sir" inDisney's Animated Storybook. However, there is a single instance in theClassic Storybookjunior novelization (which otherwise uses "it") where the Hydra is referred to as "her", suggesting that it is actuallyfemale; this is not the case in theLadybirdnovelization, despite the two books sharing much of the same text. Animal Assassin: Giant man-eating mythological monster version. Unlike his other monstrous minions, Hades doesn't apparently control the Hydra but merely creates circumstances where Hercules is bound to release and encounter the beast, with its hunger taking care of the rest. The effect is much the same though: if Hercules hadn't slain the Hydra first, his death wouldn't have looked like a murder to the other gods.

characters.name: Echidna
characters.description: A draconic Titan who is the wife of Typhon and mother of several powerful monsters. Adaptational Ugliness: Descriptions of Echidna in mythology vary, but she's often said to look like a beautiful nymph with the body of a serpent or dragon. Here, she's a monstrously hideous kaiju like her husband, though shedoeskeep the serpentine dragon motif. Beware My Stinger Tail: Her tail is tipped by a scorpion-like stinger, which Hercules uses to his advantage by forcing her to sting herself.Echidna:[snarls in pain]Watch where you point that thing! Card-Carrying Villain: Echidna is a proud monster and delights in causing death, destruction, and chaos; wanting her children to follow in her footsteps. Draconic Abomination: Echidna is an ancient draconic goddess with four legs, two arms, a mane of fur covering her torso, horns, a pair of small wings, and a humanoid face.

characters.name: Typhon
characters.description: A draconic Titan who once fought Zeus for control of the cosmos and was trapped beneath a mountain. Arch-Enemy: Typhon was this to Zeus long before Hades became consumed by envy. Draconic Abomination: Typhon is a five-headed draconic monster — with four heads serving as arms — with tentacles for legs, and is an ancient and powerful monster who once battled Zeus for control of the cosmos. The Dreaded: True to the mythology, Typhon is feared by mortals and gods alike. When he’s freed, the reaction from the Athenians is aMass "Oh, Crap!". Happily Married: Typhon is married to fellow draconic Titan Echidna, with whom he had several monstrous offspring.

characters.name: Medusa
characters.description: A Gorgon who lives in Gorgon Land. Despite her monstrous appearance, Medusa is a nice, insecure girl who just wants to have friends. Adaptational Nice Girl: Depending on which myth you believe, Medusa was born a Gorgon and she enjoyed petrifying people. Here, she feels lonely and just wants real friends. Become a Real Boy: Between Hades' offer to turn into a human at daylight and Aphrodite's offer to wear a pair of magical glasses which won't turn people into stone, Medusa chooses the former. Cute Monster Girl: Even though she believes she's hideous, her human-like characteristics and her desire to have friends makes her seem cute. Deadly Gaze: Her gaze turns everyone into stone.

characters.name: Orthos
characters.description: A two-headed cyclops who became Hercules' first enemy. Adaptation Species Change: In the original Greek myth, Orthos was a two-headed dog who guarded Geryon's cattle and the brother of his three-headed counterpart Cerberus. Here, he's a two-headed cyclops. Blue Means Cold: His skin color is blue. Cyclops: A cyclops with two heads. Diet Episode: In their debute episode, Echidna is tired of their slovenly lifestyle and puts them on a strict diet of only eating royalty or heroes to get them out of their lair and get in shape.

characters.name: The Sphinx
characters.description: Exclusive to theHercules Dynamitecomics, the Sphinx is a terrifying, huge winged cat monster more dangerous than the Titans. It took every god, including Hades, to exile her to Egypt, but she learned ancient arts there and returned to kidnap the pantheon one by one, draining their powers and establishing her own rule. All Your Powers Combined: After draining the gods' power she can make use of all of them, and does so. Came Back Strong: She learned ancient magic during her exile to Egypt, which made her stronger than ever and a completely unknown force to the Greek Gods. The Dreaded: So evil and powerful that all the gods fear her, and it took all of them to defeat her the last time. Eviler than Thou: Stronger than the Titans and evil enough for Hades to team up with the pantheon to defeat her.

characters.name: Zeus and Hera
characters.description: Hercules' biological parents. The King (Zeus) and Queen (Hera) of the Olympian Gods. Adaptational Heroism:In Hera's case, it's played completely straight. In the myths, she was a vindictive and jealous woman who was not particularly kind to her own children, let alone her stepsons including Hercules, whereas in the film she's his loving biological mother.Zeus is a bit different, in that certain mythic depictionsdidhave him as something of a doting father to his children, such as Artemis. Interestingly, the movie shows Zeus as nothing but a loving father and husband without any of his negative traits from the Greek myths, while the TV series demonstrates that he still has some of his less-favorable qualities, like a brash temper when slighted, though hislecherousqualities are still understandably left out. Overall, both the movie portrayal and the TV show iteration or Zeus are shown to be SAINTS compared to his original mythological counterpart. In theDisney's Animated Storybookversion ofHercules, there is a minigame where the player has to identify the constellations over Zeus' temple, one of which mentions his transformation into a swan and fateful meeting with the princess Leda. While the game mentions that he did it to "surprise" Leda, it omits his seducing of her forobvious reasons. In Hera's case, it's played completely straight. In the myths, she was a vindictive and jealous woman who was not particularly kind to her own children, let alone her stepsons including Hercules, whereas in the film she's his loving biological mother. Zeus is a bit different, in that certain mythic depictionsdidhave him as something of a doting father to his children, such as Artemis. Interestingly, the movie shows Zeus as nothing but a loving father and husband without any of his negative traits from the Greek myths, while the TV series demonstrates that he still has some of his less-favorable qualities, like a brash temper when slighted, though hislecherousqualities are still under

characters.name: Hermes
characters.description: An Olympian God, serving as a royal messenger of the Gods. Adaptational Job Change: In the original mythology, he was in charge of guiding spirits to the afterlife, while in the Disney version the spirits seem to be pulled to the afterlife automatically. Adaptational Ugliness:No offense to Paul Shaffer intended, of course,but he hardly looks like the beautiful, blond youth Hermes was said to be in the myths. Adaptational Wimp: Hermes was able to borrow (or steal) Hades' helm of darkness anytime he wanted in the myths. In the movie, he's easily captured and subdued by Pain and Panic to be dragged off into the Underworld once the Titans storm Mount Olympus. Amazing Technicolor Population: Hermes has blue skin.

characters.name: Hades
characters.description: The main antagonist and ruler of the Underworld.He has a self-demonstrating pagehere. Abhorrent Admirer: To Aphrodite in the animated series. She's off-put by both his creepiness and the fact that she's already married to Hephaestus, though he never seems to quite get the hint. Adaptational Comic Relief: In the original mythology, Hades is dour, humorless, andThe Stoicto the point that his very rare tears are described as being of iron. This version of Hades acts like a fast-talking used car salesman and has a bitter or snarky quip for virtually everything. Interestingly, the creators did originally envision Hades as a dark and serious villain, butJames Woods' audition was such a hit with them that they overhauled the character to make him humorous. Adaptational Villainy: Hades was not an enemy of Hercules in the original myths, nor did he ever try to overthrow Zeus. He was generally one of the more reasonable deities, and actually helped Heracles in one of his Twelve Labors by loaning him Cerberus. Here, he's the slimy and treacherousBig Bad. Adaptational Wimp: Downplayed. In the myths, Hades' rule wasn't assigned by Zeus but drawn by fate, and they interacted as equals, neither trying to undermine the other one's authority.

characters.name: Poseidon
characters.description: God of the seas, earthquakes, and horses, Poseidon is the middle brother of the trio of rulers and is content with his realm and tends to stay out of mortal affairs...usually. Adaptational Heroism: A minor one, as in the myths it wasPoseidonwho was involved in an attempt to overthrow Zeus, while here it was Hades. Ascended Extra: In the TV series and other media. Expy: Similar toJason Alexander's previous Disney role as Abis Mal inAladdin, Poseidon is basically a demigod version ofGeorge Costanza. God Is Flawed: When he tried to make marine mammals, they kept drowning until he also invented blowholes.

characters.name: Ares
characters.description: The Olympian God of war and the founder of Sparta. Abusive Dad: He treats his sons Fear and Terror poorly. Putting aside his understandable rage at their idiocy, he also hates their interest in playing a trivia board game as opposed to going to war. Adaptational Badass: Despite being aLoser Deityhe is not harmless. "Hercules and the Big Games" saw him and Athena easily defeat Echidna after Hercules failed to defeat her. Adaptational Ugliness: The Greek Ares was said to be aBrainless Beauty, being surprisingly handsome for a brutish god of war. Here, he's a short, pudgy old man. He actually more closely resembles his Roman equivalent Mars, who was typically depicted as an older bearded man, although stillstrong and handsome. Adaptational Villainy: He only briefly appears in the movie in one or two scenes, at the party and during the charge against the Titans. Neither of these indicates anything about the villain that the animated series cast him as.In the 2024 comic series he feigns sympathy towards Herc, but only as part of a scheme to trick him into creating a pointlessForever Warbetween humans and centaurs.

characters.name: Athena
characters.description: The Olympian Goddess of Wisdom and War and the patron of Athens. Adaptational Wimp: For the most part she is aFaux Action Girl, unlike her mythological counterpart. Age Lift: The original myths maintain that Athena was never a child—she wasborn fully formed from Zeus' skull. In the TV series, she and Ares are briefly shown as babies in a flashback and it's said they've been fighting since they were "waddling, toddling gods". Amazing Technicolor Population: Athena has blue skin. Amplifier Artifact: Ibid, Athena's pet owl, can grant anyone genius levels of knowledge and intellect if he sits on their head.

characters.name: Aphrodite
characters.description: The Olympian Goddess of Love and Passion. Adaptational Heroism: The Aphrodite of the Greek myths acted pettily just like the other Olympians (for instance, the story ofEros And Psychestarted when she tried to enactDisproportionate Retributionfor someone complimenting Psyche's beauty more than her own). The Disney version, naturally, behaves in a much more family-friendly manner. Amazing Technicolor Population: Aphrodite has pinkish-purple skin. Ascended Extra: In the TV series and other media. The Burlesque of Venus: In the episode "Hercules and the Dream Date", Aphrodite appears to a bramble of flowers miraculously appearing, a beaming light, her rather cheesy introduction song topped off with, wait for it, stepping out of a giant clam that floated in.

characters.name: Apollo
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: His body and hair are purple from head to toe. Power Trio: He, Ares, and Athena were the first Olympians to charge into battle when the Titans were released. In the animated series, Ares and Athena tend to be the Gods he is seen with the most.

characters.name: Artemis
characters.description: Adaptation Personality Change: A minor one as while still the Goddess of the Wild in the myths she was the patron of hunters, while here she's aGranola Girlwhohateshunters. Deep South: Despite being a Greek Goddess, she speaks with a heavy southern accent. Not surprising as she's voiced byReba McEntire. Friend to All Living Things: Wherever she goes, animals are drawn to her wanting to give her affection. This also affects Hercules when he becomes her champion briefly. Gaia's Vengeance: As Goddess of the Wild, this is her role as she protects the wilds from hunters. She briefly gives this assignment to Hercules in order to protect theCalydonian Boars. Psycho Ex-Girlfriend: Artemis has a gender inversion with Orion who she broke up with due to his crazed hunter behavior which nearly got smited by Zeus.

characters.name: The Muses
characters.description: The Muses are five lovely goddesses whose domain lies in the arts, and they sing the tales of ancient Greece in a gospel choir style. They claim to be Hercules' biggest fans, narrating the movie and singing in four of the six songs. All-Knowing Singing Narrator: Boy, they can sing amazing stories! Big Beautiful Woman: While the other muses are rail thin like Megara, Thalia is not and is still gorgeous. Big Fun: Thalia is the chubbiest of the Muses, and she tends to serve as the comic relief of the group. Fitting, since she's the Muse of Comedy. Breaking the Fourth Wall: In the beginning of the movie, they decide the narrator is too serious and grim, so they decide to take over in telling the tale.Calliope:We'll take it from here, darling!(bats eyelashes)Narrator:You go, girl.

characters.name: The Fates
characters.description: The Three Fates are the quaternary antagonists. These three sisters share one eye, which they use to see the future. They also determine the deaths of mortals, cutting a mortal's Thread of Life to send them to the Well of Souls in the Underworld. They have extreme psychic abilities, knowing everything that has happened, is happening and will happen, and are an authority above the gods in this respect, though the one thing they cannot do is kill a god. Abhorrent Admirer:Clotho towards Hades, which is something he exploits to get her to tell him the future. "My fate is in yourlovelyhands."Atropos is also this to Hercules in the episode "Hercules and the Tapestry of Fate". Clotho towards Hades, which is something he exploits to get her to tell him the future. "My fate is in yourlovelyhands." Atropos is also this to Hercules in the episode "Hercules and the Tapestry of Fate". Adaptational Wimp: Their shared eye can see more than everyone else's in the entire universe put together, and yet in this rather loose take on the myths they lack the ability to affect the future, unlike the original mythology, as they never write down and dictate destiny, and only cut the threads of people who have died of unrelated causes to them. Notably, Hades never once attempts to convince them to influence the things that are yet to come, in a way favorable to him.Zigzagged in the animated series, which introduces them weaving the Tapestry of Fate and shows that they do indeed write down and dictate destiny. Notably, Hades never considers to manipulate this for himself untilafterHercules and Icarus do it themselves to get concert tickets and he briefly swaps places with Zeus in the cosmic scheme of things. However, it's shown that they still aren't totally infallible in this aspect as they're taken by surprise in a later episode when Atlantis is accidentally knocked off the tapestry and thus destroyed.

characters.name: Trivia
characters.description: The God of trivial information and where three-roads-meet. All of the Other Reindeer: Virtually everyone on Olympus hates spending time with him, as he goes on and on about whatever factoid he considers relevant. Ares even bemoans how a simple bowling game can last longer than the average war. Hades also refused to invite him to his pool party scam for this reason, though this ended up wrecking the scheme in the end. Trivia still considered the snub a rather large insult. Amazing Technicolor Population: Trivia has purple skin. He's a god, you know. Ancient Grome: Trivia didn't exist in Greek mythology. Trivia was theRomanportrayal of the goddess Hecate, who in this continuity is a seperate god. Bait-and-Switch: Trivia catches Zeus doing this when he 'thanks' him helping Hercules. Zeus offers to let Trivia sit next to him at lunch, by pointing out that depending on which side of Zeus he sits it can mean either power and respect or 'Pass the Condiments'. Which from Zeus expression he clearly was intending the latter.

characters.name: Hecate
characters.description: Demigoddess of the night and witchcraft, Hecate appears in two episodes of the TV series with her eyes on Hades' throne. Like Hades, she has minions of her own, talking winged wolves named Canis and Lupis. Adaptational Villainy: Her mythological counterpart was a neutral-to-benevolent goddess, while here she's as bad as Hades. Adaptational Wimp: While still skilled in magic, her mythological inspiration was a full-fledged goddess who Zeus himself said had no peers; in the series she's a scheming demigoddess with little sway among the Olympians or Hades himself. Ambition Is Evil: Her goal in life is to rule the Underworld instead of Hades. Better the Devil You Know: Her open goals about what she plans to do once she has control of the Underworld means that even though Hades is also an enemy of the heroes, they are incentivized to stop her from usurping him.

characters.name: Demeter
characters.description: Goddess of nature, the harvest, and the seasons. Demeter is warm and friendly most of the time, but isn't one to make angry. Amazing Technicolor Population: She is green from head to toe unless someone angers her enough to make her bloom in autumn colors. Ascended Extra: In the TV series and other media. Beware the Nice Ones: Demeter is caring and understanding towards most of her subjects, but when she learns Pan hasn't given heranyofferings and created a temple praising himself, she gets so furious she blooms in fall colors and sends Nemesis after him. Unrelated in the Adaptation: As a side effect of making Zeus and Hera's relationship more family-friendly, Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades are not Demeter's brothers.

characters.name: Hestia
characters.description: Goddess of the hearth, home, and family, everyone loves Hestia, and she does her best to get along with everyone in return. She's also a fantastic chef. All-Loving Hero: She loves everyone and is loved in return by everyone (except Hades). Cool Big Sis: To Hera and Demeter, who are always thrilled to see Hestia. Endangered Soufflé: A running gag in her focus episode is her desserts being ruined. Supreme Chef: Everyone, even Hades, loves her food.

characters.name: Nemesis
characters.description: Ancient Grome: Not her, but an episode she appears in features the Romans and the Greek Gods adopting their Roman counterpart names (All except Hades, whowouldn't even name his dog his Roman name). Casting Gag: She's voiced byLinda Hamilton, whoseStar-Making Roleis being ina franchise about a robot that will stop at nothing to kill its target, much like how Nemesis will stop at nothing to smite her targets. Nemesis' ability to form weapons from her arms even brings to mindThe T-1000. Disproportionate Retribution: Sheisthe Demigoddess of Vengeance after all. Though all of her punishments even for minor slights and those who didn't deserve it are to smite with extreme prejudice. She was ready to smite Phil only because she didn't know Pan intentionally made him king so as to avoid her wrath as well as willing to smite Icarus when he was playing a god for the Romans. Intimidating Retribution Service: She runs the Infernal Retribution Service and is just as terrifying as theTrope Namer. Shapeshifter Weapon: She can form her arms into any weapon to smite those who'd disrespect the gods.

characters.name: Odin
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: Has blue skin. Eyepatch of Power: King of the Norse gods, and is missing an eye, like in mythology. Horny Vikings: Wears the stereotypical horned helmet associated with the Vikings.

characters.name: Thor
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: Appears with purple skinned. Shock and Awe: Thor commands thunder and lightning.

characters.name: Loki
characters.description: Amoral Talent Agent: Just as Hades was based on used car salesmen, Loki here is characterized like a sleezy Hollywood agent. Cain and Abel: His plots against his brother Thor to make sure the gods fail come Ragnarok.

characters.name: Pain and Panic
characters.description: Pain and Panic are two shape-shifting imps who are minions of Hades and provide comic relief. They are bothveryloosely based on Deimos and Phobos from the Greek Myths, though their attitudes and personalities certainly fit their names; with Panic constantly being high-strung and nervous, and Pain is calmer, but more prone to injury, both from himself and others. The show would eventually clarify that they are spirits from Pandora's Box. Adaptational Villainy: Pain and Panic compared to Deimos and Phobos, who they were both very loosely based on. While neither of their original counterparts were exactly good guys, they were the sons of Ares and definitely weren't evil lackeys. In fact, Heracles worshiped Phobos as a god and had him depicted on his shield. Ironically, Phobos and Deimosdoappear in the animated series asFear and Terror, but they are as against Hades as Herc is. Adaptational Wimp: In the Greek Myths, Deimos (who Pain is based on) was the Greek God of Terror and Phobos (who Panic is based on) was the very personification of fear brought on by war. In the movie, they're watered down into bungling comic relief lackeys for Hades. Adaptation Name Change: A few productions of the stage musical change up their names; in the German version, they're Karl and Heinz, while the West End production renames them Bob and Charles. And There Was Much Rejoicing: Both watch in glee as their abusive boss Hades is dragged into the river Styx.

characters.name: The Titans
characters.description: The Titans are the overarching antagonists, portrayed as four elemental monsters who terrorized Ancient Greece. They were the physical manifestation of the element they controlled. There's Lythos, the Rock Titan; Pyros, the Lava Titan; Hydros, the Ice Titan; Stratos, the Tornado Titan; and... the Cyclops, who doesn't get an element. Hercules: The Animated Series— hewing somewhat closer to Greek Mythology — included several less-monstrous Titans such as Kronos, Rhea, Prometheus, Atlas, and Briares; and also categorized Typhon and Echidna as Titans. Abusive Parents: Kronos never makes a proper appearance in the series, but Zeus does mention Kronos trying to eat him as in the original myths. Abusive Precursors: The opening song states that before the Olympians ruled, the Titans were the gods in charge, and they made Earth a cruel place to live. Adaptational Abomination: Mixed withAdaptational Ugliness, the Greek Titans were sapient and humanoid beings, being more akin to a different faction of gods. Here the titans are otherworldly elemental monsters withBizarre Alien Biology.

characters.name: Prometheus
characters.description: The namesake of Prometheus Academy. This Titan was the one responsible for giving the gift of fire to humanity. Unfortunately, Zeus captured and chained him to a rock for all eternity. Or until Hercules frees him, whichever comes first. Deadpan Snarker: Suffice to say, by the time Herc comes to rescue him, Prometheus is so done with his punishment that he regularly snarks at the eagle who comes to dine on his liver everyday. Nice Guy: He saw humanity needed fire and gave it to them. Years later, he remains this, being an affable and kind guy.

characters.name: Circe
characters.description: Circe is a enchantress who desperately searches Greece for a boyfriend, but her high standards usually lead to any potential suitors being transformed into animals. Adaptational Villainy: Zig-zagged. In the original myth, while she transformed every man he came to her island as pigs, she still helped Odysseus to return home and gave him advices. Here, she's a shallow character who has extremely high expectations about her ideal boyfriend and mistreats those who don't live up to them. Affably Evil: Befitting her status as an enchantress, she remains charming even at her most wicked. Artifact of Doom: Her magic scepter, which she uses to seduce other men and also, to turn them to animals once she's bored with them. Beauty Is Bad: The beautiful, alluring enchantress who plays theBig Badin her debut appearance. The narrator himselfLampshadesher wicked beauty.

characters.name: Neurosis
characters.description: A one-shot imp minion of Hades seen in "Hercules and the Tiff on Olympus", Neurosis was called in to attack Hercules' mind and make him doubt himself. Chromatic Arrangement: He's yellow compared to Pain's purple and Panic's green. Meaningful Name: Like his fellow imps, Neurosis' name hints at his state of being—he's incredibly anxious and can pass the trait onto others. Nervous Wreck: Perpetually stressed out and can inflict this state on others. Sixth Ranger: Acts as a one-off version of this, being a third imp to Pain and Panic's duo.
